1| package alert
2| 
3| import "time"
4| 
5| // escalate walks an alert up the pager ladder. Each rung waits its
6| // ack window; an unacknowledged page moves to the next rung with the
7| // elapsed context attached. The ladder is short by design - two rungs
8| // and then the whole rotation - because long ladders teach people
9| // that someone else will answer first.
10| func (e *escalator) escalate(a Alert) {
11| 	for _, rung := range e.ladder {
12| 		if e.page(rung, a) {
13| 			return
14| 		}
15| 		time.Sleep(rung.ackWindow)
16| 	}
17| 	e.pageAll(a)
18| }

1| package alert
2| 
3| // dedupe collapses repeated raises of the same alert key into one
4| // open incident. The first raise creates the incident; repeats bump
5| // its count and freshness without re-notifying, and resolution closes
6| // the key so the next raise starts clean. Flapping keys - resolve and
7| // re-raise inside the cool-down - get a widening cool-down instead of
8| // a fresh notification each cycle, which is what keeps a bouncing
9| // check from paging the rotation every few minutes all night.
10| func (d *deduper) raise(key string, a Alert) bool {
11| 	if inc, open := d.open[key]; open {
12| 		inc.bump(a)
13| 		return false
14| 	}
15| 	d.open[key] = newIncident(a)
16| 	return true
17| }
18| 
19| // resolve closes the key. If the key re-raises inside its cool-down
20| // the incident reopens with a widened cool-down instead of a fresh
21| // notification, and the widening resets only after a full quiet
22| // window - flap history does not amnesty itself.
23| func (d *deduper) resolve(key string) {
24| 	if inc, open := d.open[key]; open {
25| 		inc.close(d.now())
26| 		delete(d.open, key)
27| 	}
28| }
